title: Systems and automation for nonprofits | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs consolidates nonprofit donor lists, volunteer schedules, and program tracking spreadsheets into one system and automates the repetitive work.
intro: Nonprofits often keep records in more places than they intend to. Donor history sits in Neon CRM or Bloomerang, the finance side in QuickBooks, volunteer sign-ups in Google Sheets or Volgistics, event registrations in Eventbrite, and program outcomes in a spreadsheet each program manager maintains separately. Reconciling gifts against deposits, preparing a grant report, or answering a board question about a program means pulling from several of these by hand.

Creosote Labs consolidates that into one system of record and builds the internal tools around it. A typical project connects the donor database to QuickBooks so gifts and deposits match without a monthly cleanup, replaces the program spreadsheets with a single tracking tool, and automates volunteer reminders, pledge follow-up, and the recurring reports the board and funders expect. We document the system and hand it over to staff.
projects: A program tracking tool that replaces per-program spreadsheets and reports outcomes in the format each funder requires.
A gift reconciliation automation that matches donor database entries against QuickBooks deposits and flags the differences.
A volunteer scheduling system that handles sign-ups, shift reminders, and hours reporting.
A pledge follow-up automation that sends reminders on a schedule and records responses in the donor database.
A grant calendar that tracks application deadlines, report due dates, and restricted fund balances in one place.
A monthly board dashboard that assembles financials, fundraising totals, and program numbers without manual copying.

faqs.q: Do we have to switch off our current donor database?
faqs.a: Usually not. Projects generally connect the existing donor database and accounting software rather than replace them. Whether a tool should be replaced is one of the questions the operations review answers.

Engagements begin with a one-day operations review at $3,000, which produces a written assessment and a quote for each recommendation. Implementation is quoted from that review at a fixed price, with no hourly billing.

faqs.q: What happens to the system after the project ends?
faqs.a: It belongs to the organization. We document how it works, train the staff who will use it, and hand it over so that it runs without us.
